In the Name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

By those who drag forth with violence (al-Nazi'at gharqan). Masruq said: they are the angels who extract the souls of the children of Adam. This is the narration of Abu Salih and 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas.

Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali, may Allah honour his face, said: they are the angels who extract the spirits of the disbelievers and the unbelievers. [[As it stands in the manuscript.]]

Ibn Mas'ud said: it means the souls of the disbelievers, which the Angel of Death extracts from their bodies from beneath every hair, from beneath the fingernails and the soles of the feet. Then he separates them and returns them into the body after they have been extracted, until, when they are about to come out, he returns them into the body. This is his treatment of the disbelievers. Muqatil said: they are [the Angel of Death] and his helpers, who extract the soul of the disbeliever as a many-pronged iron hook (safud) extracts wool from wet wool, so that his soul comes out like one drowning in water.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: their spirits are extracted, then drowned, then burned, then cast into the Fire. Mujahid said: it is death, which extracts souls. Al-Sudi said: it is the soul when it is drawn to the chest. It was also said: the disbeliever sees his soul at the time of extraction as though he were drowning. Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ibn Kaysan, Abu 'Ubayda and al-Akhfash said: they are the stars that are pulled from horizon to horizon, rising and then setting. 'Ata' and 'Ikrimah said: they are bows (qisiy). It was also said: they are raiders, archers. The meaning of the verse is:

"By those who draw forth in violent drawing, like the one who draws the bowstring when he pulls it to its utmost extent [ ... ] [[A word unreadable in the manuscript.]] that is at the blade, wrapped around it. The inner membrane of an egg-shell is called gharqa, and by gharqan he meant extreme exertion in drawing. It encompasses all of its interpretations."

وَالنَّاشِطاتِ نَشْطاً (By those who release gently, al-Nashitat nashtan). Ibn 'Abbas said: it means the angels who ease out the soul of the believer and seize it, as a hobble (iqal) is loosed from the foreleg of a camel when it is untied. Al-Farra' related this view and then said: what I have heard from the Arabs is that they say: "anshatat" and "ka'annama unshita min 'iqal"; and "rabatuha nashtan," the one who ties is "nashit"; and when you tie the rope on the camel's foreleg, you have "nashatahu" and you are "nashit"; and when you untie it, you have "anshatahu" and you are "munshit."

It is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas: they are the souls of the believers at death, which are eager to leave, for no believer is present at death without Paradise being shown to him before he dies. He sees in it likenesses of his family and his wives among the houris, and they call him to it. So his soul eagerly yearns to go out and come to them.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib said: they are the angels who ease out the spirits of the disbelievers between the skin and the nails, until they bring them out from their bellies with anguish and grief.

Mujahid said: it is death, which eases out the soul of a human being. Al-Sudi said: when it is eased out from the feet. 'Ikrimah and 'Ata' said: they are the lubricants (al-adhan). Qatadah and al-Akhfash said: they are the stars that move from horizon to horizon, that is, they go away. It is said: "Our donkey is nashit (moving), it moves from town to town," meaning it goes away. And wild cows are called nawashit because they go from place to place. Al-Tirimmah said:

"Has there been, by the allied horses, anyone you knew
Other than the ruins of the nawashit, left in fear?"

Worries also make their owner move (tanshitu), Hamyan ibn Qahafa said:

"My worries have become such that they move the places,
Sham for me at times, and at times the middle [of the land]."

Al-Khalil said: al-nashṭ and al-inshat are your pulling of something toward yourself until it is loosened. [[Al-nashṭ is binding tight, and al-inshat is loosening, Taj al-'Arus.]]

وَالسَّابِحاتِ سَبْحاً

'Ali said: they are the angels who carry the spirits of the believers swiftly.

Al-Kalbi said: they are the angels who seize the spirits of the believers like one who swims in water: at times he dips and at times he rises. They take it gently, gradually, then leave it until it rests. Mujahid and Abu Salih said: they are the angels who descend from the sky swiftly, as one says of a noble horse: "sābih" when it speeds up in its running. It was also said: they are the horses of the raiders. Imru' al-Qays said:

"Swift, when the weary ones were raising dust
Over the pebbled ground, the trampled one."

Qatadah said: they are the stars, the sun and the moon. God the Exalted said: "Each in an orbit they swim" (Yasin 40). 'Ata' said: they are the ships.

فَالسَّابِقاتِ سَبْقاً Mujahid and Abu Rawq said: they drive the son of Adam toward good and righteous action. Muqatil said: they are the angels who race with the spirits of the believers to Paradise. Ibn Mas'ud said: they are the souls of the believers that race toward the angels who take them, having already seen the joy, longing for the meeting with Allah, His mercy and His honour. 'Ata' said: they are the horses. Qatadah said: the stars race one another in their course.

فَالْمُدَبِّراتِ أَمْراً means the angels.

Abu al-Husayn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Tayyib informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Hafs informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalaf told us, saying: Abu Nu'aym told us, saying: al-A'mash told us, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, who said: Four govern the affairs of the world: Jibril, Mika'il, the Angel of Death and Israfil (peace be upon them). As for Jibril, he is entrusted with the winds; as for Mika'il, he is entrusted with rain and plants; as for the Angel of Death, he is entrusted with seizing souls; and as for Israfil, he descends with the command to them.

يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الرَّاجِفَةُ: means the first blast, by which everything quakes and moves. تَتْبَعُهَا الرَّادِفَةُ: this is the last blast, and between them is forty years. Qatadah said: they are two cries; the first causes everything to die by the permission of Allah, and the other brings everything to life by the permission of Allah. Mujahid said: يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الرَّاجِفَةُ means the earth and mountains are shaken; تَتْبَعُهَا الرَّادِفَةُ when the sky is split and the earth and mountains are carried, and they are crushed with one crushing (فَدُكَّتا دَكَّةً واحِدَةً). 'Ata' said: al-Rajifa is the Resurrection and al-Radifa is the Raising. Ibn Zayd said: al-Rajifa is death, and al-Radifa is the Hour. The root of rajifa is sound and movement, and from it comes "al-arajif" (rumours), because of the agitation of voices through them. Everything that follows something and comes after it has radifahu (followed it).

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Harun al-Hadrami told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Arafa told us, saying: Qabisa ibn 'Uqba told us, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil, from al-Tufayl ibn Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: When a quarter of the night had passed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would rise and say: "O people, remember Allah, remember Allah. The Rajifa has come, followed by the Radifa; death has come with what is in it, death has come with what is in it." [89] [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 4/53.]]

The scholars differed regarding the response to the oath. Some grammarians of Kufa said: its response is implied, meaning: "You will surely be resurrected and surely be called to account." Some grammarians of Basra said: it is His words: "Indeed in that is a lesson for whoever fears" (79:26). It was also said: there is inversion in the speech, its intended sense being: "On the day the Rajifa quakes, followed by the Radifa... by the drawers forth with violence."

قُلُوبٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ واجِفَةٌ: fearful. Mujahid: trembling. Al-Sudi: moving from their places; its parallel is إِذِ الْقُلُوبُ لَدَى الْحَناجِرِ (Ghafir 18). Al-Mu'arrikh: anxious. Qutrub: fleeing in alarm. Yaman: neither calm nor still. Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala: agitated. Al-Mubarrad: disturbed, from the palpitation of motion; it is said: "wajafa al-qalb wa wajaba," so it beats (yajifu and yajibu), with wujuf, wajib, and wujub.

أَبْصارُها خاشِعَةٌ يَقُولُونَ: meaning these deniers of the Resurrection among the polytheists of Mecca, when it is said to them: "You will be resurrected after death."

إِنَّا لَمَرْدُودُونَ فِي الْحافِرَةِ: that is, to the first state and the beginning of the matter, returning alive as we were before our life. It is from the saying of the Arabs: "rajaʿa fulan ʿala hafiratih," when one returns from where he came. A poet said:

"Returned to the former state, with baldness and grey hair?
God forbid such folly and shame."

It is said: "al-bu'd 'inda al-hafir" and "'inda al-hafira," meaning at the hastened stage, at the beginning of the matter and its first onset. And "the people met and fought at the hafira," meaning at the first word.

Abu Bakr al-Jamshadi informed us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Qati'i informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim told us, saying: 'Umar ibn Marzuq told us, saying: 'Imran al-Qattan informed us, saying: I heard al-Hasan say: "We shall be returned to the world and become living as we were." A poet said:

"I swore I would not forget you, so know,
Until people return to the hafira."

Some said: al-hafira is the earth in which their graves are dug, so it was named hafira, meaning mahfura (dug), like His words: "water gushing forth" (86:6) and "a pleasant life" (69:21). It was also said: the earth was named hafira because it is the place where hooves settle, as the foot was named "ard" (earth) because it is upon the earth. The meaning of the verse: "We return and walk upon our feet." This is the view of Qatadah. Ibn Zayd said: al-hafira is the Fire, and he recited: "That would then be a losing return" (79:12). He said: it is one of the names of the Fire, and its names are many.

أَإِذا كُنَّا عِظاماً نَخِرَةً: the people of Kufa and Ayyub read "nakhira" with an alif (ناخرة), which is the reading of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, his son, Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr, Ibn Mas'ud and his companions. The two are dialects according to most linguists, like: "al-tama' and al-tami', al-bakhl and al-bakhil, al-fara and al-fari, al-jadhr and al-jadhir." They distinguished between them, saying: "al-nakhira" is the decayed, and "al-nakhira" (ناخرة) is the hollow through which the wind passes and makes a sound (yakhurr).

قالُوا: meaning the deniers: تِلْكَ إِذاً كَرَّةٌ خاسِرَةٌ: a losing return. Allah the Exalted said: فَإِنَّما هِيَ زَجْرَةٌ: a cry and a blast, واحِدَةٌ فَإِذا هُمْ بِالسَّاهِرَةِ: meaning the surface of the earth; they will be on the face of the earth after having been in its belly. The Arabs call the wilderness and the surface of the earth "al-sahira." The leading linguists said: they named it so because in it is the sleep of animals (sahhara them), describing it by what is in it. Ibn 'Abbas and the exegetes cited the verse of Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt:

"In it is the flesh of the sahira, and the sea,
And what they have, for them, abides."

That is, for them are land and sea. Imru' al-Qays said:

"And you met after its sorrow,
So the sahira became tight upon you because of it."

Abu Dhu'ayb said:

"They pass over the sahira, as if its heat
And its darkness were the dark night's shadows."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Ibn Lamhan told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Jihad told us, from Abu Sinan, from Abu al-Minya: فَإِذا هُمْ بِالسَّاهِرَةِ is a mountain near the Holy House in Jerusalem. Al-Walid ibn Muslim related from 'Uthman ibn Abi al-'Atika: فَإِذا هُمْ بِالسَّاهِرَةِ is the open plain between the mountain of Hassan and the mountain of Ariha, which Allah extends as He wills. Sufyan said: it is the land of Syria. Qatadah said: it is Hell.

Mujahid said: يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الرَّاجِفَةُ means the earth and mountains are shaken; تَتْبَعُهَا الرَّادِفَةُ when the sky is split and the earth and mountains are carried, and they are crushed with one crushing (فَدُكَّتا دَكَّةً واحِدَةً). Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Harun al-Hadrami told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Arafa told us, saying: Qabisa ibn 'Uqba told us, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil, from al-Tufayl ibn Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: When a quarter of the night had passed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would rise and say: "O people, remember Allah, remember Allah. The scholars differed regarding the response to the oath. Some grammarians of Kufa said: its response is implied, meaning: "You will surely be resurrected and surely be called to account." "Returned to the former state, with baldness and grey hair?
God forbid such folly and shame."

And what they have, for them, abides."

So the sahira became tight upon you because of it."

Abu Dhu'ayb said:

And its darkness were the dark night's shadows."

Al-Sudi said: it is the soul when it is drawn to the chest. It was also said: the disbeliever sees his soul at the time of extraction as though he were drowning. It was also said: they are raiders, archers. The meaning of the verse is:

'Ali said: they are the angels who carry the spirits of the believers swiftly.

It was also said: they are the horses of the raiders. Imru' al-Qays said:

"Swift, when the weary ones were raising dust
Over the pebbled ground, the trampled one."

Qatadah said: they are the stars, the sun and the moon. God the Exalted said: "Each in an orbit they swim" (Yasin 40). 'Ata' said: they are the ships.

Muqatil said: they are the angels who race with the spirits of the believers to Paradise. Ibn Mas'ud said: they are the souls of the believers that race toward the angels who take them, having already seen the joy, longing for the meeting with Allah, His mercy and His honour. 'Ata' said: they are the horses. Qatadah said: the stars race one another in their course.

By those who drag forth with violence (al-Nazi'at gharqan). Masruq said: they are the angels who extract the souls of the children of Adam. This is the narration of Abu Salih and 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas.

Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali, may Allah honour his face, said: they are the angels who extract the spirits of the disbelievers and the unbelievers. [[As it stands in the manuscript.]]

Ibn Mas'ud said: it means the souls of the disbelievers, which the Angel of Death extracts from their bodies from beneath every hair, from beneath the fingernails and the soles of the feet. Then he separates them and returns them into the body after they have been extracted, until, when they are about to come out, he returns them into the body. This is his treatment of the disbelievers. Muqatil said: they are [the Angel of Death] and his helpers, who extract the soul of the disbeliever as a many-pronged iron hook (safud) extracts wool from wet wool, so that his soul comes out like one drowning in water.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: their spirits are extracted, then drowned, then burned, then cast into the Fire. Mujahid said: it is death, which extracts souls. Al-Sudi said: it is the soul when it is drawn to the chest. It was also said: the disbeliever sees his soul at the time of extraction as though he were drowning. Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ibn Kaysan, Abu 'Ubayda and al-Akhfash said: they are the stars that are pulled from horizon to horizon, rising and then setting. 'Ata' and 'Ikrimah said: they are bows (qisiy). It was also said: they are raiders, archers. The meaning of the verse is:

"By those who draw forth in violent drawing, like the one who draws the bowstring when he pulls it to its utmost extent [ ... ] [[A word unreadable in the manuscript.]] that is at the blade, wrapped around it. The inner membrane of an egg-shell is called gharqa, and by gharqan he meant extreme exertion in drawing. It encompasses all of its interpretations."

وَالنَّاشِطاتِ نَشْطاً (By those who release gently, al-Nashitat nashtan). Ibn 'Abbas said: it means the angels who ease out the soul of the believer and seize it, as a hobble (iqal) is loosed from the foreleg of a camel when it is untied. Al-Farra' related this view and then said: what I have heard from the Arabs is that they say: "anshatat" and "ka'annama unshita min 'iqal"; and "rabatuha nashtan," the one who ties is "nashit"; and when you tie the rope on the camel's foreleg, you have "nashatahu" and you are "nashit"; and when you untie it, you have "anshatahu" and you are "munshit."

It is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas: they are the souls of the believers at death, which are eager to leave, for no believer is present at death without Paradise being shown to him before he dies. He sees in it likenesses of his family and his wives among the houris, and they call him to it. So his soul eagerly yearns to go out and come to them.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib said: they are the angels who ease out the spirits of the disbelievers between the skin and the nails, until they bring them out from their bellies with anguish and grief.

Mujahid said: it is death, which eases out the soul of a human being. Al-Sudi said: when it is eased out from the feet. 'Ikrimah and 'Ata' said: they are the lubricants (al-adhan). Qatadah and al-Akhfash said: they are the stars that move from horizon to horizon, that is, they go away. It is said: "Our donkey is nashit (moving), it moves from town to town," meaning it goes away. And wild cows are called nawashit because they go from place to place. Al-Tirimmah said:

"Has there been, by the allied horses, anyone you knew
Other than the ruins of the nawashit, left in fear?"

Worries also make their owner move (tanshitu), Hamyan ibn Qahafa said:

"My worries have become such that they move the places,
Sham for me at times, and at times the middle [of the land]."

Al-Khalil said: al-nashṭ and al-inshat are your pulling of something toward yourself until it is loosened. [[Al-nashṭ is binding tight, and al-inshat is loosening, Taj al-'Arus.]]

وَالسَّابِحاتِ سَبْحاً

'Ali said: they are the angels who carry the spirits of the believers swiftly.

Al-Kalbi said: they are the angels who seize the spirits of the believers like one who swims in water: at times he dips and at times he rises. They take it gently, gradually, then leave it until it rests. Mujahid and Abu Salih said: they are the angels who descend from the sky swiftly, as one says of a noble horse: "sābih" when it speeds up in its running. It was also said: they are the horses of the raiders. Imru' al-Qays said:

"Swift, when the weary ones were raising dust
Over the pebbled ground, the trampled one."

Qatadah said: they are the stars, the sun and the moon. God the Exalted said: "Each in an orbit they swim" (Yasin 40). 'Ata' said: they are the ships.

فَالسَّابِقاتِ سَبْقاً Mujahid and Abu Rawq said: they drive the son of Adam toward good and righteous action. Muqatil said: they are the angels who race with the spirits of the believers to Paradise. Ibn Mas'ud said: they are the souls of the believers that race toward the angels who take them, having already seen the joy, longing for the meeting with Allah, His mercy and His honour. 'Ata' said: they are the horses. Qatadah said: the stars race one another in their course.

فَالْمُدَبِّراتِ أَمْراً means the angels.

Abu al-Husayn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Tayyib informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Hafs informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalaf told us, saying: Abu Nu'aym told us, saying: al-A'mash told us, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, who said: Four govern the affairs of the world: Jibril, Mika'il, the Angel of Death and Israfil (peace be upon them). As for Jibril, he is entrusted with the winds; as for Mika'il, he is entrusted with rain and plants; as for the Angel of Death, he is entrusted with seizing souls; and as for Israfil, he descends with the command to them.

يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الرَّاجِفَةُ: means the first blast, by which everything quakes and moves. تَتْبَعُهَا الرَّادِفَةُ: this is the last blast, and between them is forty years. Qatadah said: they are two cries; the first causes everything to die by the permission of Allah, and the other brings everything to life by the permission of Allah. Mujahid said: يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الرَّاجِفَةُ means the earth and mountains are shaken; تَتْبَعُهَا الرَّادِفَةُ when the sky is split and the earth and mountains are carried, and they are crushed with one crushing (فَدُكَّتا دَكَّةً واحِدَةً). 'Ata' said: al-Rajifa is the Resurrection and al-Radifa is the Raising. Ibn Zayd said: al-Rajifa is death, and al-Radifa is the Hour. The root of rajifa is sound and movement, and from it comes "al-arajif" (rumours), because of the agitation of voices through them. Everything that follows something and comes after it has radifahu (followed it).

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Harun al-Hadrami told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Arafa told us, saying: Qabisa ibn 'Uqba told us, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil, from al-Tufayl ibn Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: When a quarter of the night had passed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would rise and say: "O people, remember Allah, remember Allah. The Rajifa has come, followed by the Radifa; death has come with what is in it, death has come with what is in it." [89] [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 4/53.]]

The scholars differed regarding the response to the oath. Some grammarians of Kufa said: its response is implied, meaning: "You will surely be resurrected and surely be called to account." Some grammarians of Basra said: it is His words: "Indeed in that is a lesson for whoever fears" (79:26). It was also said: there is inversion in the speech, its intended sense being: "On the day the Rajifa quakes, followed by the Radifa... by the drawers forth with violence."

قُلُوبٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ واجِفَةٌ: fearful. Mujahid: trembling. Al-Sudi: moving from their places; its parallel is إِذِ الْقُلُوبُ لَدَى الْحَناجِرِ (Ghafir 18). Al-Mu'arrikh: anxious. Qutrub: fleeing in alarm. Yaman: neither calm nor still. Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala: agitated. Al-Mubarrad: disturbed, from the palpitation of motion; it is said: "wajafa al-qalb wa wajaba," so it beats (yajifu and yajibu), with wujuf, wajib, and wujub.

أَبْصارُها خاشِعَةٌ يَقُولُونَ: meaning these deniers of the Resurrection among the polytheists of Mecca, when it is said to them: "You will be resurrected after death."

إِنَّا لَمَرْدُودُونَ فِي الْحافِرَةِ: that is, to the first state and the beginning of the matter, returning alive as we were before our life. It is from the saying of the Arabs: "rajaʿa fulan ʿala hafiratih," when one returns from where he came. A poet said:

"Returned to the former state, with baldness and grey hair?
God forbid such folly and shame."

It is said: "al-bu'd 'inda al-hafir" and "'inda al-hafira," meaning at the hastened stage, at the beginning of the matter and its first onset. And "the people met and fought at the hafira," meaning at the first word.

Abu Bakr al-Jamshadi informed us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Qati'i informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim told us, saying: 'Umar ibn Marzuq told us, saying: 'Imran al-Qattan informed us, saying: I heard al-Hasan say: "We shall be returned to the world and become living as we were." A poet said:

"I swore I would not forget you, so know,
Until people return to the hafira."

Some said: al-hafira is the earth in which their graves are dug, so it was named hafira, meaning mahfura (dug), like His words: "water gushing forth" (86:6) and "a pleasant life" (69:21). The meaning of the verse is: "We shall be returned to the earth, then raised as a new creation, then returned in our graves as dead." This is the view of Mujahid and al-Khalil ibn Ahmad. It was also said: the earth was named hafira because it is the place where hooves settle, as the foot was named "ard" (earth) because it is upon the earth. The meaning of the verse: "We return and walk upon our feet." This is the view of Qatadah. Ibn Zayd said: al-hafira is the Fire, and he recited: "That would then be a losing return" (79:12). He said: it is one of the names of the Fire, and its names are many.

أَإِذا كُنَّا عِظاماً نَخِرَةً: the people of Kufa and Ayyub read "nakhira" with an alif (ناخرة), which is the reading of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, his son, Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr, Ibn Mas'ud and his companions. It was chosen by al-Farra' and Ibn Jarir for conformity with the verse-endings. The rest read it with a kasra and without the alif (نخرة), which is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim. Abu 'Ubayd said: "We chose it for two reasons: first, the great majority of people are upon it, including the people of Tihama, the Hijaz, Syria and Basra; second, we have examined the reports mentioning bones that have rotted, and we found them all with 'nakhira' (نخرة), and I have never heard 'nakhira' (ناخرة) in any of them." Abu 'Amr would argue with a third argument: he said: "Its 'tanakhur' (rotting) would be 'tankhur', but it was not done." The two are dialects according to most linguists, like: "al-tama' and al-tami', al-bakhl and al-bakhil, al-fara and al-fari, al-jadhr and al-jadhir." They distinguished between them, saying: "al-nakhira" is the decayed, and "al-nakhira" (ناخرة) is the hollow through which the wind passes and makes a sound (yakhurr).

قالُوا: meaning the deniers: تِلْكَ إِذاً كَرَّةٌ خاسِرَةٌ: a losing return. Allah the Exalted said: فَإِنَّما هِيَ زَجْرَةٌ: a cry and a blast, واحِدَةٌ فَإِذا هُمْ بِالسَّاهِرَةِ: meaning the surface of the earth; they will be on the face of the earth after having been in its belly. The Arabs call the wilderness and the surface of the earth "al-sahira." The leading linguists said: they named it so because in it is the sleep of animals (sahhara them), describing it by what is in it. Ibn 'Abbas and the exegetes cited the verse of Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt:

"In it is the flesh of the sahira, and the sea,
And what they have, for them, abides."

That is, for them are land and sea. Imru' al-Qays said:

"And you met after its sorrow,
So the sahira became tight upon you because of it."

Abu Dhu'ayb said:

"They pass over the sahira, as if its heat
And its darkness were the dark night's shadows."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Ibn Lamhan told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Jihad told us, from Abu Sinan, from Abu al-Minya: فَإِذا هُمْ بِالسَّاهِرَةِ is a mountain near the Holy House in Jerusalem. Al-Walid ibn Muslim related from 'Uthman ibn Abi al-'Atika: فَإِذا هُمْ بِالسَّاهِرَةِ is the open plain between the mountain of Hassan and the mountain of Ariha, which Allah extends as He wills. Sufyan said: it is the land of Syria. Qatadah said: it is Hell.

﴿Has the story of Moses reached you? When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Tuwa, saying: "Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed."﴾ ﴿And say: "Would you like to purify yourself,"﴾ The people of the Hijaz, Ayyub and Ya'qub read ﴿tazakka﴾ with a shadda on the zay, meaning ﴿tatazakka﴾. Al-'Abbas related the same from Abu 'Amr. Others read it without the shadda, and its meaning is "to be safe, to be reformed, and to be purified."

﴿And I guide you to your Lord, so that you fear Him.﴾ Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Habish related to us, saying: Ibn Zanjawayh informed us, saying: Muslima related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq related to us, saying: Ibn al-Taymi informed us, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, who said: Sakhr ibn Juwayriyya related to me, saying: When God Most High sent Moses (ʿalayhi al-salām) to Pharaoh, He said to him: "Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed," up to "so that you fear Him," and he will not do it. Moses (ʿalayhi al-salām) said: "O Lord, how can I go to him when You know that he will not do it?" God Most High revealed to him: "Proceed to the one you were commanded to go to, for in the heavens there are twelve thousand angels who seek to know the decree (al-qadr), yet they have not attained it nor comprehended it."

﴿So he showed him the greatest sign.﴾ That is the staff and the white hand.

﴿But he denied and disobeyed.﴾ ﴿Then he turned his back, striving.﴾ He turned away and withdrew from faith.

﴿Working corruption.﴾ ﴿Then he gathered [his people] and proclaimed.﴾ ﴿And said: "I am your Lord, the Most High."﴾ He says: there is no lord above me. It was also said: he meant that the idols are lords, and I am their lord and your lord. It was also said: he meant the leaders and chiefs.

﴿So God seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the first [life].﴾ That is, in this world and the next. In this world by drowning, and in the Hereafter by the Fire. It was also said: "the punishment" refers to his first word, which is His saying: "I know of no god for you other than me," and his last word, which is "I am your Lord, the Most High." Between them there were forty years.

﴿Indeed in that is a lesson for whoever fears.﴾ ﴿Are you, O deniers of the Resurrection, more difficult to create, or is it the heaven? He who created the heaven is able to give life to the dead.﴾ And His saying: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾.

﴿He raised its height and made it level.﴾ Its ceiling. Al-Farra' said: everything that bears some building or other is called samk, bina' and sumuk. ﴿Then He made it perfect, without flaws or cracks.﴾ ﴿And He darkened its night﴾, meaning made it dark. Al-ghatash is intense darkness, and a man who is aghtash is blind. ﴿And brought forth its forenoon﴾, meaning He made its daylight and its light manifest and evident.

﴿And after that He spread the earth.﴾ The scholars differed regarding the meaning of this verse. Ibn 'Abbas said: God created the earth with its sustenance without spreading it before the heaven. ﴿Then He turned to the heaven and made them seven heavens﴾, and then He spread the earth afterward, meaning He extended it. Ibn 'Abbas and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr said: God created the Ka'ba and placed it upon the water on four pillars two thousand years before He created the world, and the earth was spread out from beneath the House. It was also said the meaning is: "And the earth, along with that, He spread," as one says to a man: "You are a fool, and you are, besides this, of base lineage," meaning "along with this." God, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Violent, after that, of questionable birth﴾, meaning "along with that." And a poet said:

"I said to her: 'Away from me, for I am forbidden to you, and I am, after all that, wise.'" [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/205.]

meaning "along with that."

The evidence for this interpretation is the reading of Mujahid: ﴿And the earth, along with that, He spread﴾. It was also said that "after" (ba'da) means "before," as in His saying: ﴿And We wrote in the Psalms after the Reminder﴾, meaning before the Reminder, which is the Qur'an. And the Hudhali said:

"I carried my wife after 'Urwa, when Khirash escaped, and some of the greedy ones from others." They claim that Khirash escaped before 'Urwa.

The common reading is ﴿wal-arda﴾ with the accusative. al-Hasan read ﴿wal-ardu﴾ with the nominative, as a beginning with a returning pronoun. Both readings are valid in the case of the returning reference. Al-dahw means spreading and extending; from it comes "udhy al-na'āma" (the ostrich's nest), because she spreads it with her chest. One says: dahā yadhū dahwan and dahā yadhā dahyan, two dialects, like "taghā yataghū aw yataghī," "ṣaghā yaṣghū wa yaṣghī," and "maḥā yamḥū wa yamḥī," and "laḥā al-ʿūd yalḥū aw yalḥī." Whoever says "yadhū" says "dahawtu," and whoever says "yadhā" says "dahaytu."

﴿He brought forth from it its water and its pasture.﴾ Al-Qutaybi said: Observe how He indicated by two things all that He brought forth from the earth as sustenance and provision for livestock: the grass, the trees, the grain, the dates, the chaff, the firewood, the clothing, the fire, and the salt, since fire comes from wood and salt from water.

﴿And the mountains He set firm.﴾ The common reading is with the accusative, and 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd read it with the nominative. ﴿As a provision for you and your livestock.﴾ ﴿Then when the great calamity comes﴾, which is the Resurrection. It is so named because it overwhelms every great matter and submerges everything else by its immense terror, meaning it overpowers. In Arab usage, "al-ṭāmma" is that which cannot be withstood, and it is derived from the saying "ṭamma al-faras ṭamīmahā" when the horse exhausts its full effort in running.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Habish related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Imran related to us, saying: Hannad ibn al-Sarri related to us, saying: Abu Usama related to us, from Malik ibn Mughawwil, from al-Qasim al-Hamdani, regarding ﴿Then when the great calamity comes﴾: al-Hasan said: "It drives the people of Paradise to Paradise and the people of the Fire to the Fire."

﴿The Day man will remember what he strove for,﴾ meaning what he did in the world of good or evil. ﴿And Hell will be made manifest to whoever sees.﴾ ﴿As for him who transgressed and preferred the worldly life, indeed Hell will be his refuge.﴾ ﴿But as for him who feared the standing before his Lord and restrained the soul from desire, indeed Paradise will be his refuge.﴾ ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when is its arrival?﴾ When will it appear and occur? ﴿What is it to you to mention it?﴾ ﴿To your Lord is its finality.﴾ Its knowledge is with God, and you have no part in its knowledge.

'Aisha said:

The Prophet (ﷺ) continued to mention the Hour and ask about it until these verses were revealed.

﴿You are only a warner to those who fear it.﴾ The common reading is with the genitive (idafa). Abu Ja'far and Ibn Muhayṣin read "mundhiru" with tanwin. Al-'Abbas related the same from Abu 'Amr.

﴿As if, on the day they see it, they had not remained [in the world] except for an evening or its morning.﴾ It was said: in their graves. Al-Farra' said: "The 'ghashiya' has no forenoon; the forenoon belongs to the early part of the day. But this is a known usage of the Arabs, who say: 'The evening came to you, or its morrow,' meaning the last day or its first." He cited a poet from the Banu 'Uqayl:

"We attacked 'Amir in her house, with horses whose sight wearied the day for us,
at the evening of the crescent or its nightfall."

Meaning: at the evening of the crescent or the evening of the nightfall.

﴿Has the story of Moses reached you? When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Tuwa, saying: "Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed."﴾ ﴿And say: "Would you like to purify yourself,"﴾ The people of the Hijaz, Ayyub and Ya'qub read ﴿tazakka﴾ with a shadda on the zay, meaning ﴿tatazakka﴾. Al-'Abbas related the same from Abu 'Amr. Others read it without the shadda, and its meaning is "to be safe, to be reformed, and to be purified."

﴿And I guide you to your Lord, so that you fear Him.﴾ Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Habish related to us, saying: Ibn Zanjawayh informed us, saying: Muslima related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq related to us, saying: Ibn al-Taymi informed us, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, who said: Sakhr ibn Juwayriyya related to me, saying: When God Most High sent Moses (ʿalayhi al-salām) to Pharaoh, He said to him: "Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed," up to "so that you fear Him," and he will not do it. Moses (ʿalayhi al-salām) said: "O Lord, how can I go to him when You know that he will not do it?" God Most High revealed to him: "Proceed to the one you were commanded to go to, for in the heavens there are twelve thousand angels who seek to know the decree (al-qadr), yet they have not attained it nor comprehended it."

﴿So he showed him the greatest sign.﴾ That is the staff and the white hand.

﴿But he denied and disobeyed.﴾ ﴿Then he turned his back, striving.﴾ He turned away and withdrew from faith.

﴿Working corruption.﴾ ﴿Then he gathered [his people] and proclaimed.﴾ ﴿And said: "I am your Lord, the Most High."﴾ He says: there is no lord above me. It was also said: he meant that the idols are lords, and I am their lord and your lord. It was also said: he meant the leaders and chiefs.

﴿So God seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the first [life].﴾ That is, in this world and the next. In this world by drowning, and in the Hereafter by the Fire. It was also said: "the punishment" refers to his first word, which is His saying: "I know of no god for you other than me," and his last word, which is "I am your Lord, the Most High." Between them there were forty years.

﴿You are only a warner to those who fear it.﴾ The common reading is with the genitive (idafa). Abu Ja'far and Ibn Muhayṣin read "mundhiru" with tanwin. Al-'Abbas related the same from Abu 'Amr.

﴿As if, on the day they see it, they had not remained [in the world] except for an evening or its morning.﴾ It was said: in their graves. Al-Farra' said: "The 'ghashiya' has no forenoon; the forenoon belongs to the early part of the day. But this is a known usage of the Arabs, who say: 'The evening came to you, or its morrow,' meaning the last day or its first." He cited a poet from the Banu 'Uqayl:

"We attacked 'Amir in her house, with horses whose sight wearied the day for us,
at the evening of the crescent or its nightfall."

Meaning: at the evening of the crescent or the evening of the nightfall.

﴿Has the story of Moses reached you? When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Tuwa, saying: "Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed."﴾ ﴿And say: "Would you like to purify yourself,"﴾ The people of the Hijaz, Ayyub and Ya'qub read ﴿tazakka﴾ with a shadda on the zay, meaning ﴿tatazakka﴾. Al-'Abbas related the same from Abu 'Amr. Others read it without the shadda, and its meaning is "to be safe, to be reformed, and to be purified."

﴿And I guide you to your Lord, so that you fear Him.﴾ Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Habish related to us, saying: Ibn Zanjawayh informed us, saying: Muslima related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq related to us, saying: Ibn al-Taymi informed us, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, who said: Sakhr ibn Juwayriyya related to me, saying: When God Most High sent Moses (ʿalayhi al-salām) to Pharaoh, He said to him: "Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed," up to "so that you fear Him," and he will not do it. Moses (ʿalayhi al-salām) said: "O Lord, how can I go to him when You know that he will not do it?" God Most High revealed to him: "Proceed to the one you were commanded to go to, for in the heavens there are twelve thousand angels who seek to know the decree (al-qadr), yet they have not attained it nor comprehended it."

﴿So he showed him the greatest sign.﴾ That is the staff and the white hand.

﴿But he denied and disobeyed.﴾ ﴿Then he turned his back, striving.﴾ He turned away and withdrew from faith.

﴿Working corruption.﴾ ﴿Then he gathered [his people] and proclaimed.﴾ ﴿And said: "I am your Lord, the Most High."﴾ He says: there is no lord above me. It was also said: he meant that the idols are lords, and I am their lord and your lord. It was also said: he meant the leaders and chiefs.

﴿So God seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the first [life].﴾ That is, in this world and the next. In this world by drowning, and in the Hereafter by the Fire. It was also said: "the punishment" refers to his first word, which is His saying: "I know of no god for you other than me," and his last word, which is "I am your Lord, the Most High." Between them there were forty years.

﴿Indeed in that is a lesson for whoever fears.﴾ ﴿Are you, O deniers of the Resurrection, more difficult to create, or is it the heaven? He who created the heaven is able to give life to the dead.﴾ And His saying: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾.

﴿He raised its height and made it level.﴾ Its ceiling. Al-Farra' said: everything that bears some building or other is called samk, bina' and sumuk. ﴿Then He made it perfect, without flaws or cracks.﴾ ﴿And He darkened its night﴾, meaning made it dark. Al-ghatash is intense darkness, and a man who is aghtash is blind. ﴿And brought forth its forenoon﴾, meaning He made its daylight and its light manifest and evident.

﴿And after that He spread the earth.﴾ The scholars differed regarding the meaning of this verse. Ibn 'Abbas said: God created the earth with its sustenance without spreading it before the heaven. ﴿Then He turned to the heaven and made them seven heavens﴾, and then He spread the earth afterward, meaning He extended it. Ibn 'Abbas and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr said: God created the Ka'ba and placed it upon the water on four pillars two thousand years before He created the world, and the earth was spread out from beneath the House. It was also said the meaning is: "And the earth, along with that, He spread," as one says to a man: "You are a fool, and you are, besides this, of base lineage," meaning "along with this." God, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Violent, after that, of questionable birth﴾, meaning "along with that." And a poet said:

"I said to her: 'Away from me, for I am forbidden to you, and I am, after all that, wise.'" [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/205.]

meaning "along with that."

The evidence for this interpretation is the reading of Mujahid: ﴿And the earth, along with that, He spread﴾. It was also said that "after" (ba'da) means "before," as in His saying: ﴿And We wrote in the Psalms after the Reminder﴾, meaning before the Reminder, which is the Qur'an. And the Hudhali said:

"I carried my wife after 'Urwa, when Khirash escaped, and some of the greedy ones from others." They claim that Khirash escaped before 'Urwa.

The common reading is ﴿wal-arda﴾ with the accusative. al-Hasan read ﴿wal-ardu﴾ with the nominative, as a beginning with a returning pronoun. Both readings are valid in the case of the returning reference. Al-dahw means spreading and extending; from it comes "udhy al-na'āma" (the ostrich's nest), because she spreads it with her chest. One says: dahā yadhū dahwan and dahā yadhā dahyan, two dialects, like "taghā yataghū aw yataghī," "ṣaghā yaṣghū wa yaṣghī," and "maḥā yamḥū wa yamḥī," and "laḥā al-ʿūd yalḥū aw yalḥī." Whoever says "yadhū" says "dahawtu," and whoever says "yadhā" says "dahaytu."

﴿He brought forth from it its water and its pasture.﴾ Al-Qutaybi said: Observe how He indicated by two things all that He brought forth from the earth as sustenance and provision for livestock: the grass, the trees, the grain, the dates, the chaff, the firewood, the clothing, the fire, and the salt, since fire comes from wood and salt from water.

﴿And the mountains He set firm.﴾ The common reading is with the accusative, and 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd read it with the nominative. ﴿As a provision for you and your livestock.﴾ ﴿Then when the great calamity comes﴾, which is the Resurrection. It is so named because it overwhelms every great matter and submerges everything else by its immense terror, meaning it overpowers. In Arab usage, "al-ṭāmma" is that which cannot be withstood, and it is derived from the saying "ṭamma al-faras ṭamīmahā" when the horse exhausts its full effort in running.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Habish related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Imran related to us, saying: Hannad ibn al-Sarri related to us, saying: Abu Usama related to us, from Malik ibn Mughawwil, from al-Qasim al-Hamdani, regarding ﴿Then when the great calamity comes﴾: al-Hasan said: "It drives the people of Paradise to Paradise and the people of the Fire to the Fire."

﴿The Day man will remember what he strove for,﴾ meaning what he did in the world of good or evil. ﴿And Hell will be made manifest to whoever sees.﴾ ﴿As for him who transgressed and preferred the worldly life, indeed Hell will be his refuge.﴾ ﴿But as for him who feared the standing before his Lord and restrained the soul from desire, indeed Paradise will be his refuge.﴾ ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when is its arrival?﴾ When will it appear and occur? ﴿What is it to you to mention it?﴾ ﴿To your Lord is its finality.﴾ Its knowledge is with God, and you have no part in its knowledge.
